text: yes well you might be overlooking the fact there is zero safety to this flow of any sort: outliner -> get uv -> add outliner -> paint is just automatically appending the 2nd outliner to the uv where any sane program would not allow that to happen without adding a brand new uv entirely, blockbench specically does not let you paint on these outliners till you remake a uv because kinda yeah no shit it would break.
resolution: Implemented the missing topology-to-UV safety contract. Every structural mesh action (add/delete/duplicate/mirror parts, cuts, extrudes, face creation/merge, detach/merge, solidify, split quads, symmetrize, and path arrays) marks the authored paint layout stale. The host now rejects paint entry, brush/fill, program/raster restore, paint undo/redo, layer mutations, and direct paint doors while stale; the UI presents an explicit Remake Paint Atlas gate, and only that atlas-base operation unlocks painting. Autosave still saves the new mesh but refuses to overwrite or endorse the old atlas, leaves the previous paint files recoverable, removes the runtime painted-form approval stamp, and writes a durable layout.stale.json marker that restores the lock after a cold restart. Added host binding contracts and classifier regression coverage; all focused tests and the editor ReleaseFast build pass.
